name: Burg Hasegg
kurzbeschreibung: Burg Hasegg in Hall in Tirol is the birthplace of the silver thaler, featuring the iconic Mint Tower and interactive coin museum.
preis: Museum Münze Hall & Mint Tower adults approx. €11.50 (family and combi tickets available)
oeffnungszeiten: Open year-round Tuesday to Sunday 10:00 to 17:00 (shorter winter hours; closed Mondays)
beschreibung:
Overview

The landmark fortress Burg Hasegg with its distinctive twelve-sided Mint Tower rises proudly on the southern edge of the historic salt town of Hall in Tirol. Founded around 1300 to safeguard salt shipping on the River Inn, urban fortifications, and the essential river crossing, the castle gained global renown in the late 15th century. Archduke Sigmund the Wealthy and later Emperor Maximilian I relocated the sovereign mint from Meran to Hall, where in 1486 the world's first high-grade silver thaler coin – the forefather of the modern dollar – was struck. Today, the magnificently restored castle houses the renowned Museum Münze Hall, offering visitors an engaging journey through the birth of modern currency, the engineering of the first roller minting press, and aristocratic castle life.

Route & Requirements

Access to Burg Hasegg is barrier-free and convenient directly from the historic old town of Hall through the cobbled castle courtyard. The museum exhibition halls on the ground floor and the courtyard are level and wheelchair accessible; however, ascending the 45-meter-high Mint Tower requires climbing 186 historical wooden and stone steps. The tower climb demands basic physical fitness and surefootedness, but rewards visitors at the top with a breathtaking panoramic view over the medieval rooftops of Hall, the broad Inn Valley, and the rugged Karwendel mountain chain. Inside the tower, guests encounter the world's largest silver thaler coin made of pure bullion and ambient audio-visual stations. Standard comfortable walking shoes are perfectly sufficient. Handheld audio guides provide informative narration in multiple languages.

Visit & Arrival

The Museum Münze Hall and Mint Tower are open year-round from Tuesday to Sunday from 10:00 to 17:00 (April to October), with slightly reduced hours during winter. Mondays are closed. Motorists reach Hall via the A12 Inntal motorway (exit Hall Mitte) and use the Altstadt underground car park or parking right by the castle. By rail, take the S-Bahn Tirol from Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof running every ten minutes to Hall in Tirol; the castle is just a five-minute walk from the station.

Tips

Strike your very own commemorative coin on the historical screw press in the museum as a personal keepsake. Combine your tour with an afternoon stroll through the protected historic old town of Hall and a quiet pause in the traditional monastery gardens.
